title: Stateside touring with Ritchie's Rainbow: Beat talks to Cozy Powell (Beat Instrumental, January 1976)
notes: Interviewed by phone from Chicago on Rainbow's first US tour. "Currently, Cozy uses two massive 26" Ludwig bass drums custom built for him by Ludwig with extra thick shells to give the thump which is so much a part of heavy drumming. Allied to these two beasts he has two 14 x 10" top tom toms, two 16 x 16" side tom toms and a metal military snare. Cymbals are a massive range of Paiste." He neither drinks nor takes drugs, for his driving and his stamina; the set ends with his drum solo; "watch other drummers ... learn all the little tricks they've got. Then, when you've learned your technique you can go about developing your own style."

title: Career In Beats: Cozy Powell (MusicRadar, 29 June 2010)
notes: His finest moments behind the kit: Dance with the Devil, "a three-minute workout around the kit with a great groove"; a 1976 solo, "his explosive mixture of raw power (just look at the battering he gives those cymbals) and dead-eye precision".

title: Jeff Beck: "Cozy Powell and I played for about a minute ... he was my John Bonham" (MusicRadar, 2 February 2024)
notes: Beck to Classic Rock on the 1970 audition: "15 drum kits set up and one double kit in red glitter"; "His idol was John Bonham, and I guess he was my John Bonham." Rainbow's solo to the 1812 Overture with pyrotechnics.

title: "I play the drums like I drive - crazy": The epic life and tragic death of Cozy Powell (Louder, 5 April 2024)
notes: "Cozy" after the 1950s jazz drummer Cozy Cole; "never took a single drum lesson"; his first proper kit a Premier; the Birmingham scene with Plant, Bonham and Iommi; the Beck audition; Keith Emerson on his "impressive drum rig".

title: Introduction to Cozy Powell (Now Spinning)
notes: From the writer's 1996 interview: on Rising, "It featured the drums fairly heavily ... We did it very quickly, in Munich. Most of those tracks were done in 2 or 3 takes. 'A Light In The Black' was done in one take"; the Rainbow audition; Donington 1980; the Whitesnake Saints & Sinners tour and Slide It In.

title: Rainbow, Live in Munich 1977 (Olympiahalle, Munich, 20 October 1977; Rockpalast)
notes: Kill the King (zEaxow3PoO0) and Long Live Rock 'n' Roll (HDT_uqM1iqI) from the concert: at the kit at 0:21, 1:20 and 4:15 of the first, 1:15 and 2:00 of the second. Shoulder-length brown hair, a black sleeveless vest, studded wristbands, a red sparkle double kit with chrome hardware. The recording date from Wikipedia's Live in Munich 1977.

title: Rainbow, Long Live Rock 'n' Roll (promotional film, 1978)
notes: Powell at 1:02 and 3:39: brown hair cut to the collar, clean-shaven, a white sleeveless T-shirt, a chrome-shelled kit with two bass drums.

title: Long Live Rock 'n' Roll (Wikipedia)
notes: Rainbow's third studio album, April 1978; personnel: Cozy Powell, drums.

title: Slide It In (Wikipedia)
notes: Recorded 1983 at Musicland, Munich, with Cozy Powell on drums; the US remix by Keith Olsen, 1984: "Cozy Powell's drum tracks are virtually not re-recorded but instead increased its clarity into the mix".

title: Love Ain't No Stranger (Wikipedia)
notes: Coverdale and Galley's song; "drummer Cozy Powell once told the singer that 'Love Ain't No Stranger' was the best track he'd ever played drums on" (25th-anniversary booklet); personnel: Cozy Powell, drums.

title: Since You Been Gone (Wikipedia)
notes: Russ Ballard's song; Rainbow's single from Down to Earth, 1979.

title: All Night Long (Rainbow song) (Wikipedia)
notes: The single from Down to Earth, a UK number 5 in 1980; Powell left after Monsters of Rock, August 1980.
